papers.title_en: Symmetric Structure and Motivic Transformation in Melodies, Phrases, and Themes
papers.abstract_en: Transposition, inversion, and retrograde are fundamental operations in music theory, from Schoenberg's twelve-tone technique to Forte's set classes and Lewin's transformational theory, yet their use in melodies has rarely been quantified. We read a melodic line through the orbits and stabilizers of its windows of $m = 3-6$ notes under the group generated by these operations and cyclic shift. The window entropy splits into an orbit entropy (motivic vocabulary) and a within-orbit entropy normalized by orbit size (deployment), and the group elements relating windows of one orbit give the motivic transformations. In 852 keyboard pieces spanning four centuries, at least 97% of melodies have lower orbit entropy than surrogates preserving their pitch content, spectrum, or one-step transitions ($m \geq 4$). Periods differ in vocabulary and symmetry types; musical forms differ in deployment. Recurring motifs are transposed 1.6 times more often than in random permutations of their forms, and transposed by a fifth or fourth 2.8 times more often, a preference that weakens from the Baroque to the 20th century and from Bach's fugues to Shostakovich's. Folk phrases and instrumental themes are rarely symmetric (2-10%), but are 1.6-5 times more often symmetric than note rearrangements. The framework extends to any symbolic sequence with a symmetry group.

papers.title_en: What Makes a Good Audio Prompt for Zero-Shot TTS? Learning Prompt Selection from Synthesis Outcomes
papers.abstract_en: Zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) models clone a target voice from a short reference clip, commonly referred to as the prompt. In practice, the prompt has to be cut from a longer recording of the speaker, so which part to use must be chosen. To understand what makes a good prompt, we analyze hundreds of thousands of outputs synthesized by four TTS models from candidate prompts of YouTube recordings. The choice of prompt substantially changes intelligibility, naturalness and speaker similarity. Standard predicted-quality scores capture mainly the naturalness part but miss most of the intelligibility gain. We find that the models largely agree on which prompt yields the highest measured speaker similarity, but much less on which prompt yields intelligible speech. We propose a small network that learns from the outputs a TTS model produced to rank a recording's candidate prompts from their audio alone. Without synthesizing anything at selection time, it picks prompts that lower the word error rate on held-out recordings by a third (Qwen3-TTS) to two fifths (F5-TTS) relative to a randomly chosen prompt, more than predicted quality achieves and nearly as much as synthesizing a dozen test sentences from every candidate first.

papers.title_en: Bridging Neural Representations and Symbolic Semantics in Audio Classification
papers.abstract_en: Deep audio classifiers can achieve strong predictive performance, but their hidden representations remain difficult to interpret. Existing audio explainability methods often focus on input-level attribution, such as waveform segments, spectrogram regions, or acoustic features, and provide limited insight into what hidden neurons encode. Interpreting hidden neurons at the concept level can provide a more meaningful view of what an audio model learns internally. This paper investigates whether hidden neurons in audio classifiers can be associated with human-understandable symbolic acoustic concepts. A model-agnostic neurosymbolic framework is presented for analyzing the final hidden layer of audio classifiers, containing 32 neurons, through symbolic concept induction. The framework is evaluated on two audio classification settings: music genre classification using GTZAN dataset and musical instrument classification using IRMAS dataset. Results show that several hidden neurons can be associated with meaningful induced concepts, and most confirmed neuron-concept pairs are statistically supported using the Mann-Whitney U test. These findings suggest that symbolic concept induction is a promising direction for explaining latent audio representations beyond input-level attribution.

papers.title_en: Discovering Interpretable Acoustic Features in Autoregressive Voice-Cloning TTS Models
papers.abstract_en: Voice-cloning TTS models synthesize an unseen speaker's voice from brief speech prompts, but it remains unclear which acoustic properties they represent and use. We introduce a feature-based interpretability framework for autoregressive voice-cloning TTS models, analyzing features from sparse autoencoders (SAEs), PCA, and random directions via sparse probing, steering, and quantitative auto-interpretability. We focus on Qwen3-TTS and extend probing and steering to $5$ additional models to test generalization across architectures. These models encode concepts like pitch, energy, noise, and accent, but sparse prediction and steering are effective only for some concepts. Strong probing does not always translate to steering or vice-versa. SAEs are useful for sparse probing of human-labelled concepts and novel-concept discovery, while PCA is competitive for dense probing and steering. Auto-interpretability finds $684$ automatically validated SAE features in Qwen3-TTS covering speaker clusters, speaking style, and recording conditions beyond known concepts. Overall, we perform a comprehensive interpretability study of autoregressive voice-cloning TTS models.

papers.title_en: SonoWorld4D: From One Video to a 4D Audio-Visual Scene via Diffusion Synchronization
papers.abstract_en: Recent progress in visual scene generation has extended beyond static 3D scenes toward the more challenging problem of generating dynamic 4D scenes from minimal input. However, sound, despite being intrinsically coupled with dynamic objects and events, remains largely unmodeled in prior work. We introduce Video-to-4DAVScene, a new task that turns a video into an explorable, time-varying 4D audio-visual scene, and present the SonoWorld4D framework for this task. Given a monocular video, our method generates a 360 static background, reconstructs explicit motion trajectories of dynamic, sound-emitting foreground objects, and synthesizes a physically-grounded sound field consistent across multiple sources through dual-space audio diffusion synchronization. The resulting 4D scene supports real-time novel-view visual and spatial audio rendering. Evaluation on real-world dynamic scenes and a user study demonstrates SonoWorld4D generates 4D audio-visual scenes with perceptually realistic, physically grounded spatial audio consistent with scene geometry and visual content.
